newsitem.title: USA: White House urges immediate release of Lima hostages.
newsitem.headline: White House urges immediate release of Lima hostages.

text.p: The White House on Monday, welcoming the release of the Americans held hostage by Marxist guerrillas in Peru, called for the immediate release of the remaining 140 captives.

"The President welcomes the safe release of the Americans who were held hostage in Lima and renews his call for the immediate release of all who continue to be held in the Japanese Ambassador's residence," a White House statement said. The guerrillas released 225 people on Sunday, but kept 140 high-profile hostages.

Although the U.S. government has so far refused to discuss how many American hostages were being held, reports from Lima said up to seven U.S. hostages were among the group released on Sunday night after five days of captivity.

"The United States expresses its great appreciation to the government of (Peruvian) President Alberto Fujimori for the support and consideration given to the Americans who were held, to their families, and to the entire American community in Peru," the White House statement by press secretary Mike McCurry said.
"The United States will continue its close consultations with Peru, Japan, and all concerned governments on this situation," the statement said.
Despite the mass release, the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels showed no signs of giving into Fujimori's demands that they lay down their arms and free the remaining captives.
